title: Merge Overlapping Intervals
statement:
Given closed intervals `[start, end]`, merge every group that overlaps
**or touches** into one.

## Your function

```
std::vector<std::pair<int, int>>
MergeIntervals(std::vector<std::pair<int, int>> intervals);
```

`intervals` arrives in **no particular order**, and each pair satisfies
`first <= second`. Return the merged intervals sorted by start. It may be
empty.

```
[1,3] [2,6] [8,10]        ->  [1,6] [8,10]
[1,2] [2,3]               ->  [1,3]         (touching counts)
[1,10] [2,3]              ->  [1,10]        (containment)
```

## Watch out

- **Sort first** -- the merge pass only works if overlapping neighbours are
  adjacent. `std::sort` on pairs orders by `first`, then `second`.
- **Merge on `next.first <= current.second`**, not `<`: `[1,2]` and `[2,3]`
  share the point `2` and become `[1,3]`.
- **Extend with `max`, not assignment.** When a later interval is *inside*
  the current one (`[1,10]` then `[2,3]`), setting the end to `3` would
  shrink the result. Take `std::max(current.second, next.second)`.
- An empty input must return an empty vector without indexing `intervals[0]`.
